title: Collection Operations
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of collection operations using at least one correct term from the lesson.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Collection Operations** as part of **Strings, Arrays, and Collections**. Select a collection by the invariants you need—ordering, uniqueness, key lookup, or indexed access—and check the cost of transformations. Use the subtopics—Filtering and Mapping, Grouping and Partitioning, Aggregation and Reduction—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Functions, null safety, strings, and collections are the building blocks of most practical Kotlin code. Choosing the right operation reduces avoidable errors and makes behavior easier to test.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: A read-only collection reference proves that no code can mutate the underlying data.
